sub_factors.description: Foreign central banks holding major portions of foreign reserves in domestic assets, creating structural demand for treasuries.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Low Foreign Exchange Volatility & Corporate Cost Certainty
contributing_factors.mechanism: Stable exchange rates eliminate the need for costly foreign exchange hedging by domestic importers and exporters, boosting operating margins.

sub_factors.description: Low implied volatility in currency forward contracts minimizing hedging premiums for international enterprises.
Dampening pass-through effects of international commodity swings onto domestic consumer price inflation.

events.name: Distributed Grid Microgeneration & Solid-State Storage Parity
events.summary: Commercialization of safe, high-density solid-state batteries and distributed rooftop solar microgeneration turns millions of businesses and households into net-energy-producing 'prosumers', democratizing the power grid and eliminating centralized utility failure risks.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Solid-State Ceramic Electrolyte Manufacturing Breakthrough
contributing_factors.mechanism: Non-flammable solid ceramic electrolytes replace liquid organic carbonates, doubling volumetric energy density while eliminating fire hazards.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Roll-to-Roll Lithium Metal Anode Vapor Deposition
sub_factors.description: Continuous high-speed manufacturing of ultra-thin lithium metal foil anodes for solid-state cells.
Novel ceramic compounds operating stably without requiring bulky mechanical pressure containment rigs.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) & Solar Shingles
contributing_factors.mechanism: Low-cost photovoltaic roofing materials and solar windows integrate into standard building codes, turning every structure into an electricity generator.

sub_factors.description: Solar roofing tiles installed by standard roofing contractors using conventional nailing guns and snap connectors.
Infrared and ultraviolet harvesting coatings applied to skyscraper architectural glass generating daytime building power.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Automated Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Microgrid Energy Trading
contributing_factors.mechanism: Neighborhood microgrids trade surplus kilowatt-hours locally using automated smart contracts, maximizing local consumption and bypassing utility grid fees.

sub_factors.description: High-speed mesh networking protocols matching neighborhood solar generation with neighboring EV charging demand.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Regulatory Approval for Private Microgrid Interconnections
sub_factors.description: Utility commission rules legalizing direct energy trading across public property rights-of-way.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Islanding Capability & Total Blackout Resilience
contributing_factors.mechanism: Decentralized storage and generation can disconnect from the macro-grid in milliseconds during storms, maintaining uninterrupted power for local communities.

sub_factors.description: Smart residential inverters creating independent local voltage references without needing centralized generator signals.
Fast motorized breakers cutting ties to the damaged regional grid in under 16 milliseconds.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Collapse in Utility Transmission Surcharges & Retail Electricity Bills
contributing_factors.mechanism: Generating and consuming electricity on-site bypasses multi-billion-dollar transmission buildout costs, reducing retail power bills by over 60%.

sub_factors.description: Eliminating the 5-10% thermal resistance energy losses inherent in transporting electricity across hundreds of miles.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Reduction in Capital-Intensive Peaker Plant Additions
sub_factors.description: Decentralized home batteries supplying peak evening loads, rendering natural gas peaker plants obsolete.

events.name: Global Sovereign Debt Default Cascades & Bond Market Fracture
events.summary: Simultaneous sovereign debt defaults across several emerging and developed economies trigger a global run on government paper, freeze sovereign bond markets, and force emergency central bank monetization.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Unbearable Debt-to-GDP Ratios & Structural Fiscal Deficits
contributing_factors.mechanism: Decades of fiscal profligacy push public debt-to-GDP ratios beyond 130%, leaving sovereign budgets incapable of absorbing higher debt-servicing costs.

sub_factors.description: Governments relying continuously on debt issuance to finance regular entitlement and operational expenditures.
Exploding off-balance-sheet demographic entitlement liabilities consuming an increasing percentage of state tax receipts.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Global Real Interest Rate Spike & Refinancing Shock
contributing_factors.mechanism: A persistent rise in benchmark interest rates forces sovereigns to roll over maturing low-coupon debt at punishingly high yields, consuming national revenues in interest payments.

sub_factors.description: Simultaneous runoff of sovereign debt holdings from central bank balance sheets, removing the primary price-insensitive buyer.
Investors demanding steep compensation for duration risk as supply overwhelms private asset manager demand.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Sovereign-Bank Doom Loop Interconnection
contributing_factors.mechanism: Domestic commercial banks holding massive portfolios of domestic government bonds suffer balance-sheet insolvency when bond prices collapse, requiring government bailouts the sovereign cannot afford.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Regulatory Zero-Risk Weighting of Sovereign Debt
sub_factors.description: Banking regulations incentivizing banks to hold massive unhedged government bond portfolios without capital buffers.
Clearinghouses and repo markets imposing punitive haircuts on distressed sovereign collateral, drying up bank liquidity.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Breakdown in International Debt Restructuring Coordination
contributing_factors.mechanism: Geopolitical divisions between bilateral lenders, multilateral institutions, and private hedge funds prevent timely debt restructuring, leading to chaotic disorderly defaults.

sub_factors.description: Rival geopolitical powers refusing to recognize each other's debt claims or provide relief without matching concessions.
Distressed debt litigation freezing sovereign escrow payments and seizing overseas state assets.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Sovereign Bond Auction Tails & Failed Bids
contributing_factors.mechanism: Primary dealers refuse to absorb new government debt issuances without massive yield concessions, triggering failed auctions and secondary market panic.

sub_factors.description: Scheduled debt auctions failing to find sufficient bids, leaving underwriters with unwanted paper.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Foreign Central Bank Liquidation of Sovereign Reserves
sub_factors.description: Overseas central banks dumping foreign sovereign paper to defend their own collapsing domestic currencies.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Exploding Sovereign Credit Default Swap (CDS) Spreads
contributing_factors.mechanism: Soaring CDS premiums trigger automated margin liquidations across derivative books, making new sovereign debt issuance prohibitively expensive.

sub_factors.description: Quant funds dumping sovereign debt as bond market realized volatility crosses predefined risk ceilings.
Sovereign debt falling out of benchmark investment indices, triggering mandatory liquidations by conservative pension funds.

events.name: Runaway Hyperinflationary Currency Collapse
events.summary: Total loss of confidence in the domestic fiat currency driven by direct central bank deficit monetization, triggering a flight into foreign currencies and physical assets, unanchored velocity of money, and social breakdown.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Subordination of Central Bank Independence (Fiscal Dominance)
contributing_factors.mechanism: The ministry of finance forces the central bank to print currency to directly fund government payrolls and debt service, destroying monetary credibility.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Direct Monetization of Treasury Spending (Overdraft Facilities)
sub_factors.description: The treasury drawing unconstrained overdraft credit directly from the central bank without issuing marketable debt.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Political Purges of Independent Central Bank Leadership
sub_factors.description: Removal of inflation-fighting governors in favor of political appointees willing to maintain artificially low rates.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Unanchoring of Public Inflation Expectations & Velocity Explosion
contributing_factors.mechanism: Households and merchants recognize that money loses value by the hour and spend it immediately upon receipt, causing velocity of money to skyrocket.

sub_factors.description: Merchants replacing price tags multiple times a day or quoting prices strictly in foreign currencies or gold.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Panic Hoarding of Non-Perishable Real Goods
sub_factors.description: Consumers converting cash immediately into canned goods, tools, building supplies, and storable commodities.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Complete Depreciation of the Foreign Exchange Rate
contributing_factors.mechanism: The national currency plummets on foreign exchange markets, causing imported food, energy, and medicine costs to multiply exponentially.

sub_factors.description: Central bank burns through its remaining dollar/euro reserves attempting to defend the currency, leaving the peg defenseless.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Proliferation of Unofficial Black Market FX Spreads
sub_factors.description: Parallel street exchange rates trading at huge discounts relative to the official government rate.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Collapse of the Domestic Tax Collection Mechanism (Tanzi-Olivera Effect)
contributing_factors.mechanism: The time lag between tax liability assessment and actual tax collection erodes the real value of government tax revenues to near zero, compounding deficits.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Real-Terms Degradation of Assessed Tax Liabilities
sub_factors.description: Taxes paid months after assessment become worthless in real purchasing terms, eviscerating state revenues.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Flight of the Informal Economy into Barter
sub_factors.description: Businesses shifting transactions completely off-grid into cash-in-hand foreign bills or physical barter.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Spontaneous Dollarization & Rejection of Legal Tender
contributing_factors.mechanism: Merchants and workers refuse to accept the national currency as legal tender, demanding foreign currency or precious metals for goods and labor.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: De Facto Commercial Rejection of Fiat Banknotes
sub_factors.description: Shops locking doors to local currency holders and accepting only stable foreign bank transfers or cash dollars.
Public and private sector workers walking off the job unless wages are index-linked daily to foreign currency benchmarks.

events.name: Systemic Banking Panics, Contagious Bank Runs & Interbank Freeze
events.summary: Rapid digital bank runs sparked by hidden asset-liability mismatches and underwater asset books cause multiple bank failures, completely freezing interbank lending and credit availability.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Severe Asset-Liability Duration Mismatch (Interest Rate Risk)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Banks holding long-duration fixed-rate securities and low-interest loans suffer massive unrealized mark-to-market losses when benchmark rates rise.

sub_factors.description: Accounting loopholes allowing banks to hide hundreds of billions in unrealized bond losses from regulatory capital ratios.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Underestimation of Deposit Beta and Outflow Velocity
sub_factors.description: Bank models mistakenly assuming low-cost retail deposits would remain sticky despite higher market yields.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Ultra-Fast Smartphone Bank Runs & Viral Panic
contributing_factors.mechanism: Mobile banking apps and social media coordination allow depositors to withdraw tens of billions of dollars in hours, overwhelming bank liquidity buffers.

sub_factors.description: Venture capital networks and corporate treasurers coordinating simultaneous withdrawals via group communications.
Digital banking rails enabling depositors to empty accounts with a single phone click without visiting branches.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Interbank Counterparty Distrust & Repo Market Freeze
contributing_factors.mechanism: Banks suspect that peer institutions hold hidden toxic assets and refuse to lend in overnight repo markets, causing liquidity to seize up.

sub_factors.description: Forward rate agreement vs. overnight index swap spreads widening sharply, reflecting extreme counterparty credit risk.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Refusal of Private Collateral in Tri-Party Repo
sub_factors.description: Repo desks rejecting corporate debt, mortgage bonds, and non-treasury collateral, demanding solely central bank reserves.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Commercial Real Estate (CRE) & Non-Performing Loan Write-Offs
contributing_factors.mechanism: Surging borrower defaults on office towers and retail malls wipe out thin equity capital cushions at regional banks.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Heavy Concentration of CRE Loans in Regional Lenders
sub_factors.description: Mid-sized banks having over 300% of their Tier-1 capital concentrated in illiquid property loans.
Property developers walking away from underwater non-recourse mortgages, dumping vacant assets onto banks.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Deposit Insurance Fund Depletion & Regulatory Scrambling
contributing_factors.mechanism: The national deposit insurance fund is drained by early bank failures, forcing emergency industry assessments and state backstops.

sub_factors.description: Resolution costs for failed mega-regional institutions depleting insurance reserves below statutory requirements.
Regulators forced to guarantee all uninsured deposits to halt contagion, creating massive moral hazard.

events.name: Global Semiconductor & Critical Lithography Supply Embargo
events.summary: Geopolitical conflict or naval blockades in East Asia sever the global supply of advanced semiconductor wafers and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography systems, paralyzing modern automotive, consumer electronics, and computing industries.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Geopolitical Conflict or Maritime Blockade in the Taiwan Strait
contributing_factors.mechanism: Military action or a naval cordon around major chip fabrication hubs halts the export of over 90% of the world's leading-edge microchips.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Suspension of Commercial Air & Maritime Shipments
sub_factors.description: Insurance underwriters revoking coverage for maritime cargo vessels and air freight transiting the conflict theater.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Wafer Fabrication Plant Shutdowns & Power Disruptions
sub_factors.description: Submarine communications cable cuts and energy fuel blockades forcing island cleanrooms into emergency shutdowns.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Extreme Geographical Concentration of Advanced Lithography & Silicon Ingot Foundries
contributing_factors.mechanism: Single points of failure across the global chip supply chain mean that no alternative facilities can ramp up production for years.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Monopoly Bottlenecks in Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) Optics
sub_factors.description: A single specialized supplier globally capable of producing high-numerical-aperture lithography mirrors.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Concentration of Raw 300mm Silicon Crystal Ingot Facilities
sub_factors.description: Over 70% of electronic-grade hyper-pure monocrystalline silicon ingots produced in a single geopolitical zone.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Automotive & Industrial Automation Assembly Line Halts
contributing_factors.mechanism: Automakers and appliance manufacturers cannot ship multi-thousand-dollar goods due to the absence of $2 microcontroller chips, triggering mass industrial furloughs.

sub_factors.description: Multinational factories halting production lines because a single microchip component is unobtainable.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in Secondary Component Gray-Market Price Gouging
sub_factors.description: Distributors hoarding microchip inventory and reselling components at 10,000% markups.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Stoppage of AI Data Center & Cloud Computing Buildouts
contributing_factors.mechanism: Hyperscale cloud providers cancel billions in data center construction due to zero availability of enterprise GPUs and specialized networking silicon.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Freeze on Frontier AI Model Training Cycles
sub_factors.description: Tech companies unable to procure replacement accelerator cards to expand compute clusters.
Cloud giants cutting back infrastructure spending, triggering revenue downgrades across IT suppliers.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Multi-Year Lead Times for Domestic Fab Replacement
contributing_factors.mechanism: Efforts to build domestic replacement fabs take 3-5 years and hundreds of billions of dollars, leaving a multi-year economic production void.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Scarcity of Specialized Cleanroom Construction Labor
sub_factors.description: Severe shortage of certified pipefitters and engineers trained in ultra-high purity gas plumbing.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Lengthy Tool Calibration & Defect Yield Ramps
sub_factors.description: New fabs requiring years of test runs to achieve commercially viable wafer yield percentages.

events.name: Severe Stagflationary Energy & Petrochemical Price Shock
events.summary: Severe disruption to primary oil and natural gas production routes triggers a multi-fold increase in global energy prices, driving high headline inflation while crushing consumer demand and economic growth.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Closure of Critical Middle Eastern Maritime Straits (Strait of Hormuz)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Military conflict or missile strikes in the Persian Gulf shut down the transit of 20% of global petroleum liquids and LNG exports.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Drone & Anti-Ship Missile Attacks on Commercial Tankers
sub_factors.description: Militant groups striking commercial oil tankers, leading Lloyd's to declare the waterway a war-risk excluded zone.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Destruction of Coastal Desalination & Export Terminals
sub_factors.description: Kinetic strikes against crude processing and export loading berths taking millions of barrels offline.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Surge in Global Oil Prices Above $150/Barrel
contributing_factors.mechanism: Global crude oil prices spike to historic highs, immediately raising gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel prices across the world economy.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Immediate Spike in Freight Transportation Surcharges
sub_factors.description: Trucking, ocean shipping, and rail companies adding emergency fuel surcharges to all consumer goods.
Prior government emergency releases having left national strategic stockpiles at multi-decade lows with zero buffer.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Spike in Natural Gas & Electricity Tariffs
contributing_factors.mechanism: Natural gas shortages cause wholesale electricity prices to soar, forcing heavy industrial energy-intensive factories to halt production.

sub_factors.description: Chemical plants halting production of nitrogen fertilizers as natural gas feedstock costs exceed finished product prices.
Governments mandating industrial gas cuts and thermostat limits to conserve gas for residential home heating.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Crushing of Household Discretionary Purchasing Power
contributing_factors.mechanism: Consumers must allocate a major portion of their monthly paycheck to basic heating and commuting fuel, collapsing retail, dining, and travel spending.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Energy Expenditure Share Exceeding 12% of Household Income
sub_factors.description: Working families cutting all discretionary purchases to afford utility bills and commuting gasoline.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Consumer Sentiment Index Crashing to Historic Troughs
sub_factors.description: Consumer confidence surveys plummeting as consumers experience simultaneous high inflation and economic gloom.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Central Bank Policy Paralysis (The Stagflation Dilemma)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Central banks are trapped: raising rates to fight energy-driven headline inflation worsens the economic recession, while cutting rates risks fueling runaway inflation expectations.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Divergence Between Core and Headline CPI
sub_factors.description: Headline inflation surging above 9% while domestic economic output and real disposable wages shrink.
Central bankers deadlocked between hawkish inflation fighters and dovish recession preventers, confusing markets.

events.name: Sovereign Credit Rating Downgrade to Speculative / Junk Status
events.summary: Credit rating agencies strip the sovereign of its investment-grade rating, triggering mandatory bond liquidations by international institutional funds, a sharp spike in borrowing yields, and a corporate credit freeze.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Deterioration of Sovereign Debt Metrics Past Statutory Redlines
contributing_factors.mechanism: Debt-to-revenue ratios and interest expense exceeding 30% of government revenue trigger automatic rating downgrade methodologies.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Failure to Pass Credible Multi-Year Fiscal Consolidation Plans
sub_factors.description: Parliamentary gridlock blocking expenditure cuts or revenue enhancements required to stabilize the debt trajectory.
Government interest payments consuming over a third of all national tax receipts, crowding out basic governance.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Forced Fire-Sale Institutional Bond Liquidations
contributing_factors.mechanism: Institutional investment mandates prohibit holding non-investment-grade securities, compelling pension funds and sovereign funds to dump bonds indiscriminately.

sub_factors.description: Global asset managers bound by charters forcing automatic sell orders upon loss of BBB- rating.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Exclusion from Major Benchmark Bond Indexes
sub_factors.description: Ejection of sovereign paper from global aggregate bond indices, forcing passive index-tracking funds to sell.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Sovereign Ceiling Spillovers onto Domestic Corporations and Municipalities
contributing_factors.mechanism: Corporate and municipal borrowers cannot maintain a higher rating than their sovereign host, triggering widespread corporate downgrades to junk.

sub_factors.description: Healthy domestic companies having their credit ratings cut purely due to sovereign country-risk ceilings.
Domestic businesses forced to pay junk bond coupons to roll over working capital credit lines.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Domestic Currency Depreciation & Capital Outflow Pressure
contributing_factors.mechanism: Foreign investors repatriate sale proceeds into foreign currencies, causing rapid currency depreciation and importing inflation.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Accelerated Outflows by Foreign Portfolio Investors
sub_factors.description: Foreign asset managers liquidating local currency bond holdings and purchasing dollars or euros.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Widening of Foreign Exchange Swap Basis Spreads
sub_factors.description: Costs for domestic institutions to hedge currency exposure through FX swap markets becoming prohibitive.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Exclusion from Primary Central Bank Collateral Eligibility Frameworks
contributing_factors.mechanism: Foreign central banks and clearinghouses disqualify the sovereign's bonds as eligible repo collateral, cutting off liquidity to international banks holding the paper.

sub_factors.description: Foreign central banks applying 50%+ haircuts or outright bans on junk-rated sovereign paper.
Trading volumes in government bonds plummeting as primary dealers cease providing two-way quotes.

events.name: Commercial Real Estate (CRE) Debt Maturity Cliff & Fire Sale Crash
events.summary: Hundreds of billions in commercial office and retail mortgages mature during a high-interest environment with low occupancy rates, precipitating widespread property surrenders, fire sales, and heavy regional bank losses.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Permanent Shift to Hybrid Work & Office Occupancy Collapse
contributing_factors.mechanism: Structural remote and hybrid work practices leave major metropolitan office towers with 30-40% physical vacancy rates, gutting rental revenues.

sub_factors.description: Fortune 500 firms cutting office square footage by half upon lease expirations to lower fixed overhead.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Decline in Urban Downtown Foot Traffic
sub_factors.description: Downtown service economies (restaurants, dry cleaners) collapsing due to reduced commuter traffic.

contributing_factors.factor_name: The Refinancing Wall (The Maturity Cliff)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Commercial property loans issued at 3-4% interest rates face refinancing at 8-10%, turning previously profitable properties cash-flow negative.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Hundreds of Billions in Imminent Debt Maturities
sub_factors.description: Over $1.5 trillion in commercial real estate debt maturing within a compressed 24-month window.
Net operating income falling below required interest and principal debt service payments.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Collapsing Commercial Property Valuations (Cap Rate Expansion)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Capitalization rates expand to match higher benchmark yields, slicing 40-60% off appraised office building values.

sub_factors.description: The current market appraisal of office buildings falling below the principal balance of the mortgage loan.
Distressed building sales at 70% discounts establishing new low comparable valuations for entire business districts.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Borrower Strategic Defaults & Key Returns
contributing_factors.mechanism: Institutional real estate funds walk away from underwater non-recourse mortgages, returning property deeds to lending banks.

sub_factors.description: Commercial loan terms shielding parent private equity funds from personal liability upon property default.
Property owners voluntarily transferring ownership to lenders to avoid protracted bankruptcy litigation.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Municipal Property Tax Revenue Shortfalls (Urban Doom Loop)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Plummeting commercial property assessments cut municipal property tax receipts, forcing city governments to slash services and raise local taxes.

sub_factors.description: Landlords winning massive downward reassessments of property tax bases, cutting city revenues.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Municipal Budget Deficits & Public Service Cuts
sub_factors.description: Cities cutting transit, sanitation, and policing, accelerating suburban flight and downtown abandonment.

events.name: Systemic Cyberattack on Wholesale Payment Systems & Energy Grid
events.summary: Coordinated cyber warfare campaign deploying zero-day malware against high-value real-time gross settlement (RTGS) payment networks and electrical supervisory control systems, shutting down regional economic activity.

contributing_factors.factor_name: State-Sponsored Zero-Day Exploits on Interbank Core Switches
contributing_factors.mechanism: Weaponized malware compromises encrypted interbank messaging protocols, corrupting transaction ledgers and forcing central clearing offline.

sub_factors.description: Supply-chain tampering with hardware modules that sign wholesale interbank wire transfers.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Data Wiping Malware on Central Ledger Servers
sub_factors.description: Malware overwriting master transaction journals and database replicas, preventing account balance verification.

contributing_factors.factor_name: SCADA/ICS Operational Technology Disruption on Electrical Grids
contributing_factors.mechanism: Cyber intrusions trip circuit breakers at major substations, disconnecting baseload generation plants and causing regional cascading blackouts.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Remote Firmware Flashing of Protective Relays
sub_factors.description: Attackers overwriting substation protective relay firmware to trigger physical transformer burnouts.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Loss of Remote Telemetry & Supervisory Visibility
sub_factors.description: Grid operators losing real-time control room visibility, forcing blind manual islanding operations.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Paralysis of Retail Commerce & Point-of-Sale Networks
contributing_factors.mechanism: Without electricity or data networks, credit card processors and ATMs go dark, halting food, fuel, and pharmaceutical transactions.

sub_factors.description: Cell towers exhausting 4-hour battery backups, taking consumer mobile banking and merchant terminals offline.
Supermarkets and gas stations unable to pump fuel or process sales without operational electronic registers.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Disruption of Just-in-Time Logistics & Hospital Operations
contributing_factors.mechanism: Supply chain warehouses and healthcare facilities face logistical chaos and backup generator fuel rationing.

sub_factors.description: Healthcare facilities struggling to secure continuous diesel tanker deliveries to keep life-support active.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Perishables Spoiled in Refrigerated Distribution Hubs
sub_factors.description: Cold-storage grocery facilities losing cooling, destroying millions of pounds of frozen and fresh food supplies.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Extreme Economic Business Interruption Losses & Insurance Denials
contributing_factors.mechanism: Insurers invoke 'war exclusion' clauses to deny billions in cyber interruption claims, leaving businesses to absorb crippling balance sheet losses.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Invocation of Hostile Act / War Exclusions by Reinsurers
sub_factors.description: Underwriters refusing to payout business interruption policies citing state-sponsored warfare attribution.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Tens of Billions in Lost Daily National Gross Output
sub_factors.description: Direct economic output lost per day of total communications and payment paralysis.

events.name: Chronic Balance Sheet Deflationary Spiral & Liquidity Trap
events.summary: Following an asset bubble collapse, households and corporations focus exclusively on paying down debt rather than spending or investing, rendering monetary rate cuts ineffective and locking the economy in chronic deflation.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Bursting of Massive Asset Price Bubbles (Real Estate & Equities)
contributing_factors.mechanism: The sudden collapse of inflated asset values leaves private sector balance sheets underwater while liabilities remain fixed at face value.

sub_factors.description: Plummeting property valuations leaving millions of homeowners and developers with negative net worth.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Evaporation of Perceived Household Paper Wealth
sub_factors.description: The reverse wealth effect causing consumers to retrench spending as stock and home equity disappears.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Corporate Shift from Profit Maximization to Debt Minimization
contributing_factors.mechanism: Firms direct all operational cash flows toward paying off bank debt instead of expanding capacity or hiring, choking off business investment.

sub_factors.description: Enterprises cancelling new factory construction and software rollouts to conserve cash for debt amortization.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Zero Demand for Commercial Bank Loans
sub_factors.description: Healthy businesses refusing to borrow even at zero percent interest rates due to debt aversion.

contributing_factors.factor_name: The Liquidity Trap & Central Bank Inpotence at the Zero Lower Bound (ZLB)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Nominal interest rates hit zero, but falling prices push real interest rates up, making monetary policy powerless to stimulate borrowing.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Policy Rates Pinned at the Zero Lower Bound
sub_factors.description: Central banks unable to cut nominal interest rates below zero without destabilizing money market funds.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Rising Real Interest Rates Driven by Deflation
sub_factors.description: Deflation increasing the real burden of outstanding debt, making hoarding cash the rational choice.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Deflationary Expectation Entrenchment & Deferred Consumption
contributing_factors.mechanism: Households postpone purchasing big-ticket items expecting prices to be cheaper next year, resulting in falling retail sales and factory layoffs.

sub_factors.description: Consumers delaying automotive and appliance replacements in anticipation of further price discounts.
Merchants cutting prices to liquidate inventory, reinforcing deflationary psychology.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Zombie Firms & Stagnant Resource Misallocation
contributing_factors.mechanism: Banks roll over non-performing loans to bankrupt 'zombie' firms to avoid acknowledging bad debts, preventing dynamic new companies from accessing capital.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Regulatory Forbearance and Evergreening of Bad Loans
sub_factors.description: Banks issuing new credit to insolvent borrowers solely to allow them to service interest on older debts.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Suppression of Creative Destruction & Total Factor Productivity
sub_factors.description: Insolvent zombie companies depressing profit margins and soaking up labor without investing in innovation.

events.name: Severe Multi-Year Continental Crop Failure & Food Crisis
events.summary: Synchronous multi-year megadroughts and fungal crop pathogens across major global breadbaskets decimate cereal grain and oilseed harvests, causing global food price spikes, food riots, and export embargoes.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Synchronous Climate Megadroughts Across Major Breadbaskets
contributing_factors.mechanism: Persistent atmospheric heat domes and failure of seasonal monsoon rains cause synchronous harvest failures across multiple major agricultural regions.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Persistent Soil Moisture Depletion Below Wilting Point
sub_factors.description: Topsoil moisture across agricultural grain belts dropping to multi-century historic lows during spring planting.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Exhaustion of Surface Irrigation Reservoir Storage
sub_factors.description: Major river basins and agricultural reservoirs dropping below minimum operational pump levels.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Outbreak of Virulent Fungicide-Resistant Rust Blights
contributing_factors.mechanism: Novel strains of wheat stem rust (e.g., Ug99 variants) sweep across global grain belts, destroying cereal yields and overwhelming existing fungicides.

sub_factors.description: Genetically uniform commercial seed varieties offering zero biological defense against mutated spores.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Global Shortages of Triazole & Strobilurin Fungicides
sub_factors.description: Chemical synthesis manufacturing bottlenecks leaving agronomists unable to source spray treatments.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Export Protectionism & Food Nationalization (Beggar-Thy-Neighbor)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Major grain-exporting countries enact emergency food export bans to stabilize domestic retail prices, removing grain supplies from world markets.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Unilateral Export Bans on Wheat, Rice, and Soybeans
sub_factors.description: Governments enacting emergency export taxes and border blockades on staple grains.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Sovereign Panic Buying and Grain Hoarding by Import-Dependent States
sub_factors.description: Import-reliant nations purchasing grain futures contracts at any price to secure domestic strategic silos.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Livestock Herd Liquidations & Protein Shortages
contributing_factors.mechanism: Skyrocketing feed grain prices force livestock and dairy producers to liquidate breeding herds, causing a temporary meat glut followed by severe protein shortages.

sub_factors.description: Ranchers unable to afford feed grains sending breeding cows to early slaughter.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Collapse in Future Meat and Dairy Production Capacity
sub_factors.description: Depleted breeding stock taking 3-5 years to rebuild, guaranteeing multi-year high food prices.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Surge in Global Malnutrition, Civil Unrest & Political Instability
contributing_factors.mechanism: Staple food prices consuming over 50% of household incomes in developing economies sparks urban food riots and government collapses.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Urban Food Riots and Supply Depot Looting
sub_factors.description: Impoverished metropolitan populations clashing with security forces outside grain silos and supermarkets.
Millions of climate refugees fleeing desiccated agricultural rural regions toward borders.

events.name: Full-Scale Multi-Theater Trade War & Retaliatory Tariff Escalation
events.summary: Escalating tit-for-tat protectionism drives average tariff rates to 1930s-era Smoot-Hawley levels, severing integrated supply chains, depressing export sectors, and reducing global potential GDP.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Nationalist Industrial Protectionism & Unilateral Tariff Levies
contributing_factors.mechanism: Domestic political populist pressures drive governments to impose across-the-board 25-50% tariffs on imported steel, electronics, and consumer goods.

sub_factors.description: Governments using broad national defense justifications to impose sweeping tariffs on allied and rival trading partners alike.
Enacting blanket import duties on all trading partners, violating World Trade Organization commitments.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Retaliatory Counter-Tariffs Targeting Politically Sensitive Sectors
contributing_factors.mechanism: Impacted trading partners respond with targeted tariffs on agricultural exports, commercial aircraft, and luxury goods, crippling export-oriented domestic producers.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Targeting of Key Agricultural Export Belts
sub_factors.description: Foreign counter-tariffs banning imports of domestic soybeans, corn, and pork, bankrupting farmers.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Discriminatory Digital Services Taxes on Tech Giants
sub_factors.description: Foreign states levying punitive taxes on domestic software and cloud firms in retaliation for physical goods tariffs.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Non-Tariff Barriers & Bureaucratic Customs Hostilities
contributing_factors.mechanism: Customs agencies introduce deliberate delays, arbitrary phytosanitary rejections, and bureaucratic hurdles to choke off imports without formal tariffs.

sub_factors.description: Regulators abruptly revoking product safety compliance for foreign manufactured goods.
Holding foreign cargo containers in quarantine yards for weeks until perishable goods spoil.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Collapse in Global Trade Volumes & Merchant Fleet Layups
contributing_factors.mechanism: International trade volumes plummet by over 20%, leading to idle container ships, cancelled port calls, and mass layoffs in maritime and logistics sectors.

sub_factors.description: Ocean carriers anchoring dozens of mega-container ships due to collapsing cargo bookings.
Major container terminals suffering steep revenue collapses and defaulting on municipal port bonds.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Deadweight Welfare Losses & Imported Consumer Price Hikes
contributing_factors.mechanism: Tariffs are passed directly to domestic consumers as higher prices, reducing real disposable income while subsidizing inefficient domestic monopolies.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Direct Pass-Through of Tariffs to Shelf Prices
sub_factors.description: Retailers adding tariff surcharges directly onto consumer receipts for imported clothing, tools, and electronics.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Destruction of Global Comparative Advantage Efficiencies
sub_factors.description: Economies forced to produce goods locally at twice the cost of specialized foreign producers.

events.name: Critical Energy Transition Mineral Cartelization & Export Embargo
events.summary: Major mineral-producing nations form an OPEC-style cartel and impose strict export quotas and resource nationalism on refined rare earths, lithium, and cobalt, halting clean energy and defense hardware manufacturing.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Monopolistic Refining Concentration in Hostile Blocs
contributing_factors.mechanism: A single geopolitical bloc controlling over 80% of global commercial refining capacity for rare earths and battery precursors weaponizes its market power.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Heavy Rare Earth Element (HREE) Separation Monopolies
sub_factors.description: Complete foreign dominance over industrial solvent extraction separation of dysprosium and terbium.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Synthetic Graphite Anode Export Licensing Controls
sub_factors.description: Foreign ministries requiring case-by-case national security approvals to export battery anode materials.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Formation of a Critical Mineral Exporting Cartel (Lithium/Cobalt OPEC)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Major resource-holding nations coordinate export quotas, minimum export pricing, and mandatory domestic processing mandates, choking global supply.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Coordinated Production Quotas and Price Pegs
sub_factors.description: Cartel members agreeing to withhold raw lithium and cobalt from international markets to drive up global prices.
Banning the export of unrefined raw ores, forcing foreign multinationals to transfer technology to build domestic plants.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Stoppage of Electric Vehicle Battery & Wind Turbine Production
contributing_factors.mechanism: Automakers and renewable equipment manufacturers cannot procure necessary battery cells or permanent magnet generators, idling billions in assembly lines.

sub_factors.description: Wind turbine and EV traction motor assembly lines halted due to lack of permanent magnets.
Automotive battery plants operating at under 25% capacity due to cathode precursor supply shortages.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Paralysis of Advanced Defense Aerospace Systems
contributing_factors.mechanism: Military defense contractors cannot complete fighter jets, radar arrays, and precision munitions that rely on specialized rare earth alloys.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Depletion of National Strategic Mineral Stockpiles
sub_factors.description: Government defense stockpiles of samarium-cobalt magnets and titanium dwindling to zero reserve days.
Guided missile production lines halted due to lack of specialized precision actuator materials.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Extreme Commodity Price Volatility & Project Cancellations
contributing_factors.mechanism: Lithium, cobalt, and rare earth spot prices surge by 400-800%, causing private utilities to cancel grid-scale battery and renewable generation projects.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Utility Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) Re-Negotiation Failures
sub_factors.description: Clean energy developers defaulting on fixed-price PPAs as hardware costs double.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Spike in Unhedged Industrial Input Costs
sub_factors.description: Industrial electronics manufacturers facing margin collapse due to soaring raw material input prices.

events.name: Unanchored Wage-Price Spiral & Inflationary Psychology Entrenchment
events.summary: High inflation expectations become permanently embedded in labor contract negotiations and business pricing strategies, creating a self-reinforcing wage-price spiral that requires punishing recessions to break.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Mandatory Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA) Contract Indexation
contributing_factors.mechanism: Labor unions and employment agreements incorporate automatic backward-looking inflation indexation, embedding past price increases into future wage floors.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Automatic COLA Escalator Clauses Across Major Sectors
sub_factors.description: Statutory rules and collective agreements adjusting wages automatically based on trailing headline CPI.
Government workers receiving double-digit statutory wage increases, expanding public fiscal deficits.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Corporate Front-Loaded Preemptive Price Increases
contributing_factors.mechanism: Firms anticipate continuing cost increases and raise selling prices preemptively and frequently, turning inflation into an aggressive business pricing norm.

sub_factors.description: Retail software updating consumer prices weekly based on projected forward inflation estimates.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Margin Expansion Under the Fog of General Inflation
sub_factors.description: Companies utilizing widespread public awareness of inflation to raise prices far beyond actual cost pressures.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Unanchored Long-Term Household & Market Inflation Expectations
contributing_factors.mechanism: Public trust in central bank inflation targets collapses, with 5-year and 10-year inflation expectations drifting far above policy targets.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: University of Michigan Long-Term Inflation Survey Spike
sub_factors.description: Consumer surveys showing median 5-year expected inflation persistently above 5%.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: De-Anchoring of 5y5y Forward Inflation Breakeven Rates
sub_factors.description: Financial market forward inflation swap rates pricing in a permanent era of high inflation.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Labor Strike Waves & Militant Collective Bargaining
contributing_factors.mechanism: Mass union strikes across transport, logistics, and manufacturing shut down production until management concedes to double-digit pay hikes.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Synchronized National Rail and Port Walkouts
sub_factors.description: Coordinated transport strikes choking distribution until wage demands are conceded.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Pattern Bargaining Multipliers Across Secondary Sectors
sub_factors.description: High-profile union settlements in automotive and freight setting precedent for non-union service sectors.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Need for Volcker-Style Punitive Monetary Crushing
contributing_factors.mechanism: The central bank is forced to hike interest rates far above inflation rates, intentionally inducing a severe recession to break the psychological spiral.

sub_factors.description: Central bank pushing real interest rates to deeply restrictive levels regardless of economic collateral damage.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Engineered Surge in Unemployment to Quench Labor Demand
sub_factors.description: Deliberately cooling labor markets until worker bargaining power and wage demands collapse.

events.name: Sudden Stop Capital Flight & Severe Currency Depreciation Crisis
events.summary: Sudden cessation and reversal of foreign capital inflows triggers massive currency depreciation, depletion of official FX reserves, emergency interest rate hikes, and corporate foreign-currency debt defaults.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Widening Current Account Deficit & External Financing Dependency
contributing_factors.mechanism: Heavy reliance on short-term foreign portfolio capital ('hot money') to finance chronic merchandise trade deficits leaves the economy vulnerable to shifts in global risk sentiment.

sub_factors.description: An overvalued domestic currency eroding manufacturing export competitiveness while encouraging debt-fueled import surges.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Heavy Reliance on Short-Term Foreign Portfolio Inflows
sub_factors.description: Financing current account deficits through volatile liquid foreign purchases of domestic bonds rather than stable FDI.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Global Risk-Off Shock & Fed/ECB Monetary Tightening
contributing_factors.mechanism: Rising interest rates in major reserve currencies widen the yield spread in favor of core economies, prompting international investors to pull capital out of emerging markets.

sub_factors.description: Investors rapidly unwinding domestic currency carry trade positions, converting proceeds into USD and EUR.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Spike in Global VIX Risk Aversion Metric
sub_factors.description: Surging financial market volatility causing global asset managers to shed emerging market portfolio exposures.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Depletion of Central Bank Foreign Exchange Reserves
contributing_factors.mechanism: The central bank expends billions in foreign currency attempting to defend the exchange rate until reserves hit critically low levels, triggering speculative attacks.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: FX Reserve Cover Falling Below 3 Months of Imports
sub_factors.description: Official foreign currency liquidity dropping below the internationally recognized safety boundary.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Speculative Shorting of the Domestic Currency
sub_factors.description: Hedge funds and domestic corporations aggressively shorting the currency via offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs).

contributing_factors.factor_name: Corporate Foreign-Currency Debt Servicing Insolvencies
contributing_factors.mechanism: Domestic corporations with dollar-denominated debts see their loan servicing obligations in local currency explode as the exchange rate plunges.

sub_factors.description: Corporations having borrowed in US dollars without currency hedging to exploit lower nominal interest rates.
Liabilities multiplying in local-currency terms while revenues remain flat, wiping out corporate net worth.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Imposition of Emergency Capital Controls & Parallel FX Markets
contributing_factors.mechanism: Desperate authorities ban foreign currency transfers and freeze accounts, destroying foreign investor trust and spawning a black-market currency crash.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Restrictions on Capital Repatriation & Dividend Remittances
sub_factors.description: Foreign firms blocked from repatriating profits, prompting complete suspension of new foreign direct investment.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in Black Market Currency Exchange Premiums
sub_factors.description: Parallel unofficial exchange rates trading at 50-100% discounts relative to official government rates.

events.name: Severe Demographic Inversion & Working-Age Population Contraction
events.summary: Decades of sub-replacement fertility rates combined with aging populations trigger a rapid contraction in the active workforce, acute labor shortages, exploding healthcare costs, and stagnant potential GDP.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Long-Term Total Fertility Rate (TFR) Collapse Below 1.3
contributing_factors.mechanism: Sustained ultra-low fertility rates shrink successive youth cohorts, causing the school-age and entering labor force populations to plummet.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Prohibitive Costs of Childcare & Urban Housing
sub_factors.description: Young couples delaying or foregoing children due to the high costs of housing and nursery care.
Changing social expectations and lack of family-friendly workplace flexibility lowering desired family sizes.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Retirement Wave of the Bulge Generation (Baby Boomers)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Mass retirements of the largest demographic cohort deplete the skilled labor force while expanding the ranks of entitlement beneficiaries.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Net Annual Contraction of the Active Labor Force
sub_factors.description: More workers retiring each year than young entrants joining the labor pool, shrinking total hours worked.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Severe Loss of Institutional & Senior Technical Knowledge
sub_factors.description: Retiring senior engineers, managers, and specialists leaving organizational voids that cannot be filled quickly.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Explosion of the Old-Age Dependency Ratio
contributing_factors.mechanism: The ratio of retirees to active tax-paying workers drops below 2-to-1, placing an unsustainable fiscal burden on younger workers.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in State Healthcare and Long-Term Eldercare Outlays
sub_factors.description: Dementia, chronic illness, and palliative care consuming growing fractions of government budgets.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Increasing Payroll Tax Burdens on Working Cohorts
sub_factors.description: Rising social insurance deduction rates reducing young workers' take-home pay and discouraging labor participation.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Persistent Labor Shortages in Essential Domestic Services
contributing_factors.mechanism: Shortages of healthcare aides, transit operators, teachers, and service workers trigger chronic operational bottlenecks.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Hospital Bed Closures Due to Nursing Deficits
sub_factors.description: Medical wards forced to cap patient admissions because of an acute lack of qualified nursing staff.
Municipal bus and train networks paring schedules due to driver shortages, stranding suburban commuters.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Decline in Aggregate National Savings & Asset Decumulation
contributing_factors.mechanism: Retirees spend down accumulated pensions and liquidate financial assets, reducing domestic capital available for corporate investment.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Net Selling of Equities and Real Estate by Retirees
sub_factors.description: Older households liquidating investment portfolios to fund retirement living, suppressing asset valuations.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Structural Decline in National Potential GDP Growth Rates
sub_factors.description: Long-term potential economic growth dropping below 1% due to negative labor force expansion.

events.name: High-Yield Corporate Debt Market Freeze & Cascade Default Wave
events.summary: Credit spreads on speculative-grade corporate debt widen to crisis levels, shutting companies out of debt refinancing and precipitating a wave of corporate bankruptcies and debt liquidations.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Over-Leveraged Corporate Balance Sheets from Low-Rate Regimes
contributing_factors.mechanism: Years of ultra-loose monetary policy led private equity and lower-tier corporations to accumulate unsustainable amounts of debt.

sub_factors.description: Companies loaded with 7x-8x debt-to-EBITDA ratios with thin operational cushions to absorb interest rate increases.
Mass issuance of debt with floating coupons and no maintenance covenants leaving companies vulnerable to rate resets.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Sharp Widening of High-Yield Option-Adjusted Spreads (OAS)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Investors demand high risk premiums to hold junk debt, driving borrowing yields above 12-15% and pricing risky borrowers out of primary markets.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Junk Bond Spreads Blowing Past 1,000 Basis Points
sub_factors.description: Credit risk premiums surging to recessionary highs as bond default probabilities jump.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Primary Junk Bond Market Issuance Halts
sub_factors.description: Underwriting banks unable to syndicate new bond deals, forcing borrowers into distressed rescue financings.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Fallen Angel Downgrades Overwhelming High-Yield Capacity
contributing_factors.mechanism: A wave of multi-billion-dollar BBB-rated corporate issuers are downgraded to junk status, overwhelming the high-yield market's absorption capacity.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Forced Selling by Investment-Grade Mandated Funds
sub_factors.description: Hundreds of billions in downgraded corporate debt dumped on the market simultaneously.
Broker-dealers refusing to inventory downgraded paper, causing bond prices to crater well below intrinsic recovery value.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Spike in Corporate Chapter 11 Filings & Bankruptcy Restructurings
contributing_factors.mechanism: Inability to roll over maturing debt forces dozens of large retailers, industrials, and telecoms into corporate bankruptcy.

sub_factors.description: Lack of liquid bankruptcy lenders willing to fund operations during court reorganization, forcing Chapter 7 liquidations.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Depressed Creditor Recovery Rates Below 25 Cents on the Dollar
sub_factors.description: Senior lenders recovering low fractions of principal, inflicting steep losses on institutional bondholders.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Mass Corporate Layoffs & Capital Expenditure Halts
contributing_factors.mechanism: Distressed companies implement emergency cost-cutting, freezing capital expenditures and laying off tens of thousands of workers, accelerating the recession.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Rapid Job Cuts Across Distressed Highly Leveraged Sectors
sub_factors.description: Private-equity-backed firms executing emergency headcount reductions to stave off immediate liquidation.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Cancellation of Supplier Invoices & Trade Credit Defaults
sub_factors.description: Defaulting enterprises failing to pay vendor bills, triggering secondary insolvency contagion among small business suppliers.

events.name: Strategic Maritime Chokepoint Blockade & Global Freight Disruption
events.summary: Simultaneous closure or severe restriction of key maritime waterways (Suez Canal, Panama Canal, Strait of Malacca) reroutes global merchant shipping, doubling voyage times, spiking freight rates, and causing widespread manufacturing component shortages.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Geopolitical Sabotage or Military Closure of Maritime Canals
contributing_factors.mechanism: Attacks by regional militias, drone strikes, or maritime mining force commercial shipping lines to divert away from vital shortcuts.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Missile and Unmanned Surface Vessel Attacks in the Red Sea
sub_factors.description: Militias targeting commercial container vessels, forcing ships to bypass Suez and transit around the Cape of Good Hope.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Severe Drought Curtailing Panama Canal Freshwater Locks
sub_factors.description: Climate droughts lowering Lake Gatun levels, cutting daily Panama ship transits by over 40%.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Surge in Transit Days & Global Shipping Route Detours
contributing_factors.mechanism: Rerouting around Africa adds 10 to 14 sailing days per voyage, soaking up effective fleet capacity and creating container imbalances.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Severe Global Absorption of Effective Container Fleet Capacity
sub_factors.description: Longer voyages tying up 15-20% of global container ship capacity at sea, creating sudden shortages.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Explosion in Bunker Fuel Consumption & Voyage Costs
sub_factors.description: Vessels burning thousands of additional tons of bunker fuel to maintain delivery schedules, raising operating costs.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Skyrocketing Ocean Freight Rates & War-Risk Insurance Premiums
contributing_factors.mechanism: Spot container shipping rates surge from $1,500 to over $8,000 per 40-foot box, alongside a tenfold increase in marine insurance hull premiums.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI)
sub_factors.description: Spot container rates multiplying as global importers enter bidding wars for scarce cargo space.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in War-Risk Hull Insurance Surcharges
sub_factors.description: Underwriters charging 1% of total vessel replacement value per transit for ships navigating contested waters.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Port Congestion & Container Equipment Imbalances
contributing_factors.mechanism: Delayed ship arrivals bunch up at destination ports simultaneously, overwhelming gantry crane capacity and stranding empty containers in consumer markets.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Vessel Anchorage Queues at Destination Deepwater Terminals
sub_factors.description: Dozens of ships idling offshore waiting for open berths, adding weeks to cargo delivery timelines.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Empty Container Accumulation in Import Destinations
sub_factors.description: Empty boxes stranded in Western ports while Asian manufacturing hubs suffer container deficits.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Downstream Factory Stockouts & Delayed Retail Deliveries
contributing_factors.mechanism: Just-in-time manufacturing plants run out of sub-assemblies, forcing automotive and electronics plant shutdowns, while seasonal goods arrive past their retail window.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Factory Idling Due to Missing Critical Components
sub_factors.description: Manufacturing facilities pausing assembly lines due to parts stuck on rerouted maritime vessels.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Retailer Markdowns on Past-Season Seasonal Merchandise
sub_factors.description: Holiday merchandise arriving months late, forcing retailers to write down inventories at deep losses.

events.name: Sovereign Pension System Insolvency & Mandatory Fiscal Bailout
events.summary: National public and municipal pension systems exhaust reserve trust funds due to demographic aging, poor investment returns, and benefit promises, forcing massive central government bailouts that crowd out public investments.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Exhaustion of Statutory Public Pension Trust Fund Reserves
contributing_factors.mechanism: Annual benefit payouts permanently exceed incoming payroll tax contributions, consuming reserve assets until funds face statutory benefit-cut cliffs.

sub_factors.description: Social security reserve funds reaching zero balance, triggering mandatory statutory benefit reductions unless bailed out.
Pension funds assuming unrealistic 7.5% annual investment returns while actual returns deliver 3-4%.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Unfunded Liabilities at State and Municipal Pension Schemes
contributing_factors.mechanism: Sub-national governments face multi-trillion-dollar pension deficits, forcing cities to divert operational tax revenues toward pension contributions.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Pension Contributions Exceeding 30% of Municipal Budgets
sub_factors.description: Local city taxes swallowed entirely by legacy pension promises for retired civil servants.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Municipal Bankruptcy Filings and Chapter 9 Restructurings
sub_factors.description: Cities filing for bankruptcy protection to adjust unaffordable legacy pension and retiree healthcare liabilities.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Mandatory Sovereign General Revenue Emergency Bailouts
contributing_factors.mechanism: Politicians cannot allow millions of elderly citizens to suffer a 20-30% cut in pension benefits, passing multi-billion-dollar general-fund bailouts.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Direct Transfers from the National General Fund
sub_factors.description: Legislatures appropriating hundreds of billions annually from income taxes to cover pension shortfalls.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Emergency Issuance of Sovereign 'Pension Relief' Bonds
sub_factors.description: Treasuries issuing dedicated sovereign debt to recapitalize insolvent public retirement schemes.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Crowding Out of Public Capital Expenditures & R&D
contributing_factors.mechanism: Ballooning pension transfers consume available discretionary budget space, forcing governments to cancel infrastructure upgrades, education, and scientific research.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Cancellations of Highway, Rail, and Water Infrastructure Projects
sub_factors.description: Capital budgets deferred indefinitely to preserve entitlement benefit payments to older voters.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Freezing of University and Basic Scientific Research Grants
sub_factors.description: Public research councils cutting funding for scientific labs to feed pension entitlement outlays.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Generational Political Grievance & Taxpayer Resistance
contributing_factors.mechanism: Younger working generations face higher taxes to fund benefits they doubt they will ever receive, sparking political protests and tax avoidance.

sub_factors.description: Political polarization pitting younger workers paying high taxes against older cohorts receiving protected benefits.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Emigration of Skilled Youth to Lower-Tax Jurisdictions
sub_factors.description: Young professionals moving abroad to avoid heavy payroll deductions earmarked for legacy pension deficits.

events.name: Massive Domestic Brain Drain & High-Skilled Capital Flight
events.summary: Economic mismanagement, heavy taxation, lack of opportunity, or political instability prompt an exodus of doctors, software engineers, research scientists, and entrepreneurs, permanently eroding national innovation and productivity potential.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Severe Wage Stagnation & Professional Compensation Gaps
contributing_factors.mechanism: Large pay disparities for specialized professions compared to foreign jurisdictions create strong economic incentives for talented individuals to emigrate.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: 3x-5x Salary Differentials in Competing Foreign Markets
sub_factors.description: Foreign employers offering multiple times the domestic take-home pay for physicians, software engineers, and AI researchers.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Punitive Marginal Tax Rates on Professional Incomes
sub_factors.description: High top marginal tax rates and social surcharges reducing the net rewards of advanced specialized labor.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Decaying University & Laboratory Research Infrastructure
contributing_factors.mechanism: Cuts in domestic R&D grants and outdated laboratory equipment prompt academic researchers to move their projects to better-funded foreign universities.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Starvation of University Equipment & Research Budgets
sub_factors.description: Academic laboratories unable to afford modern supercomputers, sequencing tools, or cleanroom access.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Foreign Headhunting Campaigns for Principal Investigators
sub_factors.description: Foreign research institutes offering multi-million-dollar startup packages to poach leading research teams.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Exodus of Technology Founders & Venture Capital Relocations
contributing_factors.mechanism: High-growth tech entrepreneurs incorporate abroad to access deeper capital pools, friendly regulations, and liquid exit markets.

sub_factors.description: Startups transferring their corporate domicile and intellectual property to foreign innovation hubs.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Venture Capital Mandates Requiring Foreign Relocation
sub_factors.description: Global VC funds conditioning term sheets on executive leadership moving to tech hubs like Silicon Valley or London.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Healthcare System Collapse Due to Medical Professional Flight
contributing_factors.mechanism: The departure of surgeons, specialists, and nurses causes wait times to explode and hospital departments to close, degrading public health outcomes.

sub_factors.description: Regional hospitals unable to find oncologists, anesthesiologists, and pediatric surgeons.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in Elective Surgical Wait Times Past 12 Months
sub_factors.description: Patients suffering extended delays for essential care, resulting in deteriorating health and work absenteeism.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Permanent Erosion of National Total Factor Productivity (TFP)
contributing_factors.mechanism: The cumulative loss of the top 5% of intellectual talent depresses the nation's capacity for domestic innovation and patent generation.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Steep Decline in Domestic Patent Applications
sub_factors.description: Annual patent filings dropping as top innovators file inventions through foreign corporate sponsors.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Shrinking High-Tech Export Share of Total Merchandise Trade
sub_factors.description: The national economy regressing toward low-value-added primary commodities and basic assembly work.

events.name: Sovereign Treasury Bond Auction Failure & Debt Saturation Spike
events.summary: Massive government borrowing schedules overwhelm private market absorption capacity, leading to a failed sovereign debt auction, primary dealer balance sheet saturation, and an emergency yield spike across all debt instruments.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Explosive Sovereign Debt Issuance Schedules (Supply Glut)
contributing_factors.mechanism: Treasury floods the market with hundreds of billions in new bonds each month to finance wide deficits, exceeding private market demand.

sub_factors.description: Borrowing needs expanding beyond historical precedent, overwhelming the absorptive capacity of capital markets.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Refinancing Wave Concentrated in Long-Duration Paper
sub_factors.description: Treasuries issuing heavy supplies of 10-year and 30-year paper that institutional investors are unwilling to absorb.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Primary Dealer Balance Sheet Saturation & Regulatory Constraints
contributing_factors.mechanism: Primary dealer banks reach regulatory leverage limits (SLR) and cannot absorb unsold auction paper without breaching capital adequacy rules.

sub_factors.description: Bank capital rules penalizing primary dealers for warehousing large inventories of sovereign debt on balance sheets.
Underwriters sitting on unsold bond inventories, forcing them to submit low bids at subsequent auctions.

contributing_factors.factor_name: The 'Auction Tail' Blowout & Uncovered Auction Climax
contributing_factors.mechanism: A scheduled treasury auction receives bids below the offered amount or clears at an unprecedented yield tail, triggering panic across secondary debt markets.

sub_factors.description: The high yield at auction clearing far above the pre-auction trading price, signaling weak investor appetite.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Collapse in Indirect Bidder Participation (Foreign Central Banks)
sub_factors.description: Foreign reserve managers and overseas institutional investors bidding for under 40% of the auctioned tranche.

contributing_factors.factor_name: Spillover Yield Spikes into Mortgages and Corporate Borrowing
contributing_factors.mechanism: The sovereign yield spike immediately flows through benchmark rate curves, pushing 30-year residential mortgage rates and corporate debt costs to multi-decade highs.

sub_factors.sub_factor_name: Surge in Long-Term Mortgage Interest Rates
sub_factors.description: Benchmark home loan rates jumping by 200 basis points in days, shutting down residential home sales.
